insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (examples shown: ₹1.5L, ₹2L, ₹3L, ₹4L, ₹5L, ₹10L, ₹15L; Gold Plan shows up to ₹25L)

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months from the policy inception with the insurer. Claims for PEDs will be payable only after you complete 3 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 2. Speciﬁed disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy start. You can claim for these only after completing 2 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section IV. EXCLUSIONS > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (Page 5/9)
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This means you should not expect coverage for non-accident illnesses during the first month.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured by 200%, once during the policy period... such restored Basic Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made... This beneﬁt is not available for Modern Treatment
good.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > K. Automatic Restoration of Basic Sum Insured (Page 3/9)
good.explanation: Basic Sum Insured is automatically restored by 200% once in a policy year, but it can be used only for an unrelated illness/disease. The restored amount cannot be used for Modern Treatment, which can limit usefulness in some high-cost claims.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered up to 30 days before hospitalization. Diagnostic tests and consultations older than 30 days before admission will not be payable.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry in to this policy is 61 years and above. This co-payment will not apply for those insured persons who have entered the policy before attaining 61 years of age and renew the policy continuously without any break
bad.reference: Important Note : Applicable for II Coverage and Optional Covers > Point 6 (Page 5/9)
bad.explanation: A 10% co-pay applies on each and every claim if you enter the policy at age 61 years or above. This means you must pay 10% of admissible claim amounts from your pocket in addition to any non-payable items.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Basic Sum Insured Rs Limits (Rs) 1,50,000/- 2% of Basic Sum Insured maximum of Rs.5,000/- per day
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > A. Room, boarding, nursing expenses... (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited to 2% of Basic Sum Insured, capped at ₹5,000 per day (for the ₹1,50,000 Basic Sum Insured shown). Choosing a higher-priced room can lead to reduced claim payouts and higher out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Expenses relating to Associated Medical Expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > Note under A (Page 2/9)
bad.explanation: Associated medical expenses are paid only in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category if you take a higher room than allowed. This can significantly reduce reimbursement for doctor fees, nursing, and other linked hospital charges.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: ITEMS THAT ARE TO BE SUBSUMED INTO PROCEDURE CHARGES... DISPOSABLES RAZORS CHARGES... SURGICAL BLADES... GAUZE... SURGICAL TAPE...
bad.reference: Annexure/List: ITEMS THAT ARE TO BE SUBSUMED... (Page 9/9)
bad.explanation: The policy lists many consumables (e.g., gauze, surgical tape, blades) as items to be subsumed into procedure charges rather than paid as separate line items. In practice, hospitals often bill these separately, which can increase your out-of-pocket expenses if not accepted under the claim.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
bad.quote: Post Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period up to 60 days... The amount payable shall not exceed the sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of Rs.5,000/- per hospitalisation.
bad.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered up to 60 days after discharge, but are capped at 7% of hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of ₹5,000 per hospitalization. This low cap can leave you paying most follow-up medicines and consultations yourself.

bad.name: No Claim Bonus
bad.quote: In the event of a claim resulting in... At any point of time, the cumulative bonus will not be less than “zero”... the cumulative bonus granted on renewal will be “nil” or “zero”
bad.reference: Section II. COVERAGE > J. Cumulative Bonus (Special Conditions) (Page 3/9)
bad.explanation: The cumulative bonus can reduce to “nil” or “zero” on renewal if a claim occurs. This means you may lose the accumulated increase in coverage after a claim, reducing protection in later years.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only in networked Hospitals. For details of Networked Hospitals, the insured may visit www.starhealth.in or contact the nearest branch
unclear.reference: Section V. CONDITIONS > 2.B Documents for Cashless Treatment (Page 6/9)
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at network hospitals, but the policy wording does not state the number of network hospitals. The actual cashless convenience will depend on whether your preferred hospitals are in the insurer’s network.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
